cohort: The study included 607 nonpregnant women with a history of cesarean section who underwent transvaginal ultrasound measurements of the lower uterine segment.
finding: The residual muscular layer (TRM) measured by transvaginal ultrasound was significantly different between women with and without cesarean scar symptoms and those with and without CSDs, with a TRM cut-off value of 4.15 mm showing 87.8% sensitivity and 71.3% specificity for predicting CSDs.
cross-section timing: At the time of transvaginal ultrasound examination in nonpregnant women with a history of cesarean section, without specifying a time interval from the last cesarean section.
